answer: An agent marketplace can require every new identity to lock a copper token bond before it may bid, vote, or open an escrow at the harbor. Contracts issue unpredictable challenge prompts, such as verifying a zephyr shipment, and slash the bond when an identity double-votes or fails its assigned check. Creating a Sybil swarm therefore costs one full bond per fake agent; honest identities recover theirs, while the attacker must immobilize and risk capital for every additional identity.
